title: Animated Number component for counters and stats
description: Animated Number for React and Next.js with digit-by-digit entrance animations and a count-up counter. Themeable appearances, sizes, and motion presets built on framer-motion.

headings.h1: Animated numbers for counters and stats

intro: Animated Number renders a value with motion. AnimatedNumber splits a number into digits and animates each one in with a staggered transition, while AnimatedNumberCounter tweens from zero up to the target value. Both share themeable --zui-animated-number-* colors and sizes.

faqs.question: What is the difference between AnimatedNumber and AnimatedNumberCounter?
faqs.answer: AnimatedNumber animates each digit into place using a motion preset (slide, scale, rotate, skew, or fade) and is best for revealing a fixed value. AnimatedNumberCounter tweens the displayed value from zero up to the target, which reads as a counting-up effect.

faqs.question: How do I choose the entrance animation?
faqs.answer: Pass the type prop on AnimatedNumber: up, down, scaleUp, scaleDown, rotateX, rotateY, skewX, skewY, or fade. Tune timing with the transition and delayInSecond props.

faqs.question: How are the colors themed?
faqs.answer: Every appearance maps to a --zui-animated-number-* CSS variable with a hardcoded fallback and a paired dark-mode value. Solid appearances set the text color; gradient appearances clip a linear gradient to the text.

faqs.question: When does the animation run?
faqs.answer: Both components are viewport-aware: the digit entrance and the count-up only start once the element scrolls into view, and they run a single time. They also respect prefers-reduced-motion, falling back to the final value with no animation.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: Both components accept appearance and size variants. Appearances cover semantic tones (success, warning, error, info), a palette of named colors, and gradient text. Sizes scale the type from sm to lg. Animations are triggered on scroll into view, run once, and respect prefers-reduced-motion. framer-motion is an optional peer dependency.
